quotes: "Novice programmers are increasingly relying on Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate code for learning programming concepts." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: learning_or_skill_development — the techniques are designed for deeper learning and avoidance of skill degradation (PDF pp. 1–2).
quotes: "To address this issue, we conducted a systematic design exploration to develop seven cognitive engagement techniques aimed at promoting deeper engagement with AI-generated code." (p. 1)
"Therefore, to prevent skill degradation, the focus should shift toward fostering deeper cognitive engagement with AI-generated code, rather than discouraging or limiting its use." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: novice_or_learner — participants were undergraduate learners in a data-structures course (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "We recruited 82 participants (44 male, 37 female, 1 non-binary), ages 18–23 (𝑀 = 19), from an undergraduate programming course about data structures at a large public university." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: strategy_or_process_gap — learners need support with the stepwise planning, problem-solving, and algorithmic reasoning needed to use generated code rather than merely accept it (PDF pp. 2–3).
quotes: "Ideally, it would empower learners to not only understand the AI-generated code better but also to apply learned concepts to writing, extending, or modifying similar code." (p. 2)
"They must simultaneously learn conceptual knowledge, syntactic knowledge, and strategic knowledge like planning, problem-solving, and debugging [93]." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the studies measure task time, cognitive load, response accuracy, perceived understanding, and willingness (PDF pp. 9, 13).
quotes: "To compare participants’ perceived friction across techniques, we analyzed both task completion time and NASA Task Load Index (TLX) scores." (p. 9)

"In terms of the accuracy of learners’ responses to the questions prompted by each technique, for the Trace-and-Predict technique, learners were asked an average of 8.3 tracing questions (to predict values) and 3.7 short-answer questions to explain the highlighted part of the code." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — performance was scored from participants’ manually written code (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Learners’ responses to the manual coding tasks were graded using two detailed rubrics, each tailored to one of the two tasks." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: learning_or_transfer — evaluation tasks tested application of learned concepts to isomorphic tasks without AI (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "RQ1 [Performance]: How effectively do the updated cognitive engagement techniques affect the transfer of learned programming concepts to isomorphic coding tasks without AI assistance?" (p. 12)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — hierarchical pseudocode and solution decomposition organize code into subgoals and sequential decisions (PDF pp. 6, 11).
quotes: "The pseudocode is organized into subgoals, grouping several lines of code with a descriptive title." (p. 6)
"The prompt first decomposes the code solution into a hierarchical JSON, explaining decisions at the subgoal level to each line of code." (p. 11)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the workflow deliberately prevents immediate use and makes learners confront the reasoning or faults in generated code (PDF p. 15).
quotes: "In alignment with these approaches, we introduce Friction-Induced AI, wherein the AI does not allow users to use its generated solution immediately." (p. 15)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — the AI evaluates the learner’s current response and offers hints or identifies missing detail (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "Additionally, users receive feedback via an LLM prompt that checks their response, offering hints or pointing out missing detail." (p. 11)

quotes: "Instead, it engages the user in the process of generation, while challenging them (similar to Lead-and-Reveal) and providing opportunities for reflection." (p. 15)
